text: After staring down an 0-3 abyss that threatened to derail their season entirely, the Patriots joined the Rams and Cowboys in orchestrating one of Week 4's most stunning turnarounds, clawing back to 2-2 with a 29-26 upset victory over the Bills at the new Highmark Stadium—a win that Mike Vrabel deemed critical for the defending AFC East champs and one that featured Drake Maye shaking off both an early-season slide and two turnovers on Sunday to orchestrate a game-winning drive while throwing three touchdown passes, making New England the first team to win in Buffalo's brand-new building. The narrative shift has been immediate: beat writers are already debating whether the Patriots are genuinely back on track for another division title or whether this represents an overreaction to a single impressive victory, though there's no denying that Maye's clutch performance against Josh Allen and company demonstrated the kind of composure and execution the offense will need if New England has any chance of sustaining this momentum.
